description: With password protection enabled, can someone read my note hierarchy, timestamps, tags, or attachment filenames directly from the database?

conversation.content: With password protection enabled, can someone read my note hierarchy, timestamps, tags, or attachment filenames directly from the database?

answer_criteria.instruction: Correctly distinguish readable hierarchy/IDs/timestamps from encrypted tags and attachment filenames/metadata. Do not confuse attachment metadata with plaintext structural metadata.
Explain field-level rather than full-database encryption without claiming every byte is protected or inspecting a personal database.

expectation.reference_facts: MetaList uses field-level encryption, not whole-file SQLite encryption. Note IDs, parent/previous/next relationships, collapse flag, created/updated timestamps remain readable. Note bodies, accepted/proposed tags and attachment title/metadata/blob are ciphertext. Filenames and MIME type are inside encrypted attachment title/metadata, not readable as file payload metadata. Namespace/port and crypto metadata are readable. This does not hide file size or access patterns.
